create table public.teams (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table public.team_members (
  team_id uuid not null references public.teams (id) on delete cascade,
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  role text not null default 'member' check (role in ('admin', 'member')),
  primary key (team_id, user_id)
);

create table public.projects (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid not null references public.teams (id) on delete cascade,
  name text not null,
  created_by uuid references auth.users (id),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create index projects_team_id_idx on public.projects (team_id);

-- Used by the dashboard's project list.
create view public.project_overview as
  select p.id, p.name, p.team_id, t.name as team_name, p.created_at
  from public.projects p
  join public.teams t on t.id = p.team_id;

content.text:
I added `supabase/migrations/20260102000000_enable_rls.sql`. I haven't run it, because there's no database here to apply it to.

- **Access:** RLS is on for `teams`, `team_members` and `projects`.
  - Members can read their teams, those teams' members and those teams' projects.
  - Admins can add and remove members, and create, edit and delete projects.
  - Everyone else gets nothing. The `anon` role has no grants, so signed-out visitors see nothing.
- **Admin check:** Two helper functions, `private.is_team_member` and `private.is_team_admin`, do the membership lookup. They run as the function owner so the `team_members` policies don't recurse into themselves. They sit in a `private` schema, so the API doesn't expose them.
- **Project moves:** Editing a project also requires admin on the team it's being moved to, so an admin can't move a project into another team.
- **View:** `project_overview` would have bypassed RLS, because views run as their owner by default. I set `security_invoker = true` on it, so it now follows the caller's permissions. It is read-only for signed-in users.

You didn't say who can create, edit or delete teams, so I granted no write access on `teams`. The same goes for editing a member's role, since you only asked for add and remove. Clients can't create a team or make the first admin, so that has to go through the service role (for example an Edge Function or RPC). If you want clients to do it, tell me the rule and I'll add it.
